subject: Proposal: DPA incident evidence transfer & subprocessor handover timeline
messages:
From: Lisa Clark <lisa.clark@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com, acme_security_ops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Urgent: scope + handover timing for DPA incident evidence

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for taking our call this morning. Per our legal team, we need a concise proposal from Redwood clarifying:

- The earliest practical window you can produce a forensic snapshot and relevant telemetry for a limited-scope incident (specific customer IDs provided in attachment).
- What subprocessors (and their locations) will be involved if data needs to be exported for our forensics team.
- A proposed evidence-handover sequence that minimizes Prod impact and preserves chain-of-custody.

Could you include any constraints (e.g., retention, export approvals, export format) and an estimated turnaround for a locked forensic package? We attached a short template with the fields our GC expects.

[Attachment: acme_evidence_scope_request.pdf (application/pdf, 82KB)]

We need this to finalize our 72-hour escalation memo; please reply with a proposed plan and timing.

Best,
Lisa Clark
Head of Security Compliance
Acme Health Systems

-----Original Message-----
(Attachment referenced above)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Clark <lisa.clark@acmehealth.com>
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-05-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: scope + handover timing for DPA incident evidence

Lisa —

Thanks — got the template and the customer list. High-level reply here while I loop in our forensics and legal leads to get a detailed timeline:

- We can provide a read-only forensic snapshot + requested telemetry within 48 hours of a formal evidence request from Acme, assuming there are no export approvals required for third-party subprocessors.
- If the export crosses borders (even to a Redwood-hosted S3 in another region) we will need sign-off from our Data Export approver and potentially an addendum; that may add up to 24–48 hours depending on contractual commitments.
- Subprocessor disclosure: we will enumerate the subprocessor list and locations in the follow-up. We typically avoid physical handovers; we provide signed forensic exports over an encrypted transfer or via an auditor account in your tenant where applicable.

Ben (for forensics) and Kim (legal) — can you confirm whether 48 hours + up to 48h export approval is what we can commit to for Acme? Also attaching our internal checklist to speed review.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security & Trust | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
[Attachment: redwood_forensics-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 28KB)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-05-01T12:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: scope + handover timing for DPA incident evidence

Team — forwarding Acme's ask (attached). Quick needs:

1) Forensics: confirm feasible earliest forensic snapshot availability for the three customer IDs in Lisa's PDF and whether we need a full node quiesce or if a live KV-snapshot suffices (impact to latency/process). Estimate ETA in hours.
2) Subprocessors: produce a short list of subprocessors that could be implicated for data export, including region/country and whether encryption-at-rest keys are customer-managed.
3) Legal/Privacy: Kim, confirm whether cross-border export approvals require an amendment or if our existing DPA (EU–US SCCs + model clauses) covers the transfers for Acme's jurisdiction.

Acme has emphasized a 72-hour internal escalation. If we can't deliver a locked package within their timeline, we should propose staged deliverables (metadata + low-sensitivity telemetry first, forensics package next).

I don't want to overpromise — please hit reply-all with a compact plan.

Thanks,
Vanessa

--- Forwarded attachment: acme_evidence_scope_request.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-05-01T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: scope + handover timing for DPA incident evidence

Vanessa / all — quick technical confirmation and proposed handover sequence: 

- Snapshot method: For the itemized customer IDs, a consistent KV-checkpoint + read-only forensic snapshot from the serving cluster is sufficient. We do not expect to need a full node shutdown; we will use our live snapshot tooling to capture KV cache + request traces. That reduces Prod impact.
- ETA: 36 hours to produce the locked forensic package (includes snapshot creation, integrity hashing, and packaging).
- Export approvals: if Acme requests delivery to an external storage location (non-Redwood-managed), this triggers an Export Approval workflow. Typical time: 24 hours for standard EU–US documented transfers; 48 hours if legal needs SCC addendum or if keys are customer-managed and coordination is required.
- Subprocessors likely to be involved for any export/storage: Cloud object storage provider (us-east-1 region), our managed logging vendor (logs-us), and a remote analytics partner used for telemetry (telemetry-eu). I will send the full name + country list in a follow-up email (we keep that data in our subprocessor registry).

Proposed handover sequence (we will deliver these as separate artifacts):
1) Within 12 hours: Metadata summary + manifest of requested objects (no PII payloads).
2) Within 36 hours: Encrypted forensic package (sha256 hash) delivered to Acme's security SFTP endpoint (or Redwood-managed transfer for faster turnaround).
3) Within 72 hours: If export to Acme-managed cloud is requested, complete export + certification of chain-of-custody (post approvals).

Attachments included: forensics checklist and quick triage matrix.

Action items: Kim, confirm export approval lead and whether SCCs/annex suffice for Acme's country. Marissa, please prepare a short subprocessor disclosure table we can attach to the Acme reply.

Ben Carter
Principal Forensics Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_forensics-checklist.xlsx (updated)]

From: Lisa Clark <lisa.clark@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: compliance@acmehealth.com, acme_security_ops@acmehealth.com
Date: 2028-05-01T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: DPA incident evidence transfer & subprocessor handover timeline

Vanessa / Ben —

Appreciate the clear timeline and staging. The sequence you outlined looks workable for our incident response timeline. Two quick asks before we close the loop:

1) Please send the explicit subprocessor table (vendor, country, data categories) as Marissa prepares it. We need that to validate export approvals.
2) If export approval is required, can Redwood provide a contact for the Export Approver and an expected SLA for the decision?

If you can send the metadata manifest within 12 hours, we'll start internal triage and escalate the approvals path in parallel.

I'll mark this as our acute incident thread and will circulate internally. Thanks for the fast turnaround.

Best,
Lisa Clark
Head of Security Compliance
Acme Health Systems
